decisions.decision: V2-071 is stage 2 of the Repository outcome and delivers exactly three things: a real Git working copy per Increment inside the Runner's confinement, the Requirement-to-Repository association that tells the working copy what to clone, and the repair of the dead repository control scope. It does not reach any remote: no clone target is a remote this Loop writes to, no push argv can be constructed by the adapter, and the adapter has no remote-mutating code path at all. Reaching the real forge with a push stays V2-072.
decisions.rationale: The task-state's own non_goals forbid pushing, forbid making the Git working copy a domain contract, and forbid a working copy outliving its Increment. dp-v2-064 d1 already scoped stage 2 to exactly this content and d13/d14 deferred the association and the ServiceConfig.RepositoryID defect here by name. Measured: credential.helper is unset at local and global scope, so a bare git push cannot authenticate in this environment even if it were attempted, which makes the push leg a separate task with a separate credential design rather than a line of code at the end of this one.

decisions.decision: The Git port and its adapter live in internal/runner as two new files: internal/runner/sourcecontrol.go (the port interface, its value objects, its sentinel errors and its closed argv allowlist) and internal/runner/git.go (the one adapter, GitSourceControl). No new Go package is created. internal/domain gains no Git type of any kind.
decisions.rationale: Three independent measurements force this. (1) ci/components.json is a prohibited path and every internal/* package is a declared component root (internal/runner/** belongs to component "runner"); a brand-new package would be an undeclared root and V2-045's manifest surface check (internal/ci/manifest_dependencies_test.go TestManifestDependencySurface, TestDerivedGraphMatchesDeclaredNarrowings) would turn make check red on the first undeclared import edge. (2) internal/runner is already the only package permitted to start a child process -- internal/runner/forge.go states the same argument for the gh adapter -- and internal/runner/source_guard_test.go TestProcessSupervisorReferencedExactlyOnceInProviderExecutionPath exists precisely to stop a second uncontrolled spawn site appearing. (3) docs/architecture/overview.md L153 ("Git worktreeは最初のSource Control Adapterとして利用できるがdomain contractにはしない") is honoured by the port being an interface in internal/runner rather than a type in internal/domain: the domain change in this task is the Requirement-to-Repository link only, and it names no Git concept.

decisions.decision: The port is one interface, SourceControl, with seven methods, each one stage of the outcome: Version (execution-environment identifier), Materialize (independent clone plus branch), ApplyChange (write a bounded ChangeSet inside the copy), VerifyIntegrity (Git-level verification, executed), Commit, Discard, and RunProjectVerification (declared, fails closed, see d9). Its value objects are WorkingCopy, MaterializeRequest, ChangeSet/ChangeFile, IntegrityObservation, CommitObservation and ProjectVerification. The only production implementation is GitSourceControl; the fake lives in a _test.go file in the same package and is never shipped in a non-test file.
decisions.rationale: A port has to be cut where the fake is useful and where the real thing is unavoidable. The five write stages are the ones a caller (an Orchestrator, a later Provider-driven flow) wants to fake, so they are methods; the mechanism (unshare, mount, absolute git path, guarded environment) is not a caller concern and stays private to the adapter. Keeping the fake test-only mirrors the repository's existing habit: internal/runner's fakes for the Provider live in test files, and forge.go injects only a Stat hook rather than shipping a fake client. docs/architecture/validation.md L84 forbids faking git in the integration test, so the fake exists for callers of the port, never for the gate-bearing test of the adapter itself.

decisions.decision: Every git child is started from a resolved absolute path whose filepath.Base equals "git", with a closed subcommand allowlist checked before any process can exist: version, init, clone, checkout, switch, add, commit, rev-parse, status, diff, fsck, ls-files, cat-file, symbolic-ref. push, fetch, remote, submodule, config, credential and worktree are absent from the allowlist, and an argv naming one is refused. Every non-clone command carries -C <absolute working copy root> rather than a working directory, and the working copy is always produced by git clone, never by git worktree add.
decisions.rationale: The absolute-path plus basename assertion is the measured house idiom (internal/runner/forge.go L133 and L297, from V2-017 d6) and it is what stops a configuration value substituting a different binary. The allowlist is what makes the non_goal "do not push" a property of the code rather than a promise: with push absent, no code path can construct the argv, and d6's kernel measurement is an independent second guarantee. -C is required rather than preferred: ProcessSupervisor has no Dir field (internal/runner/supervisor.go L34-40) and supervisor.go is a prohibited path in this task, so the working directory must be expressed in argv. git worktree add is refused for a measured reason: a linked worktree's .git is a file pointing into the outer repository's .git, i.e. a write path outside the confined workspace, whereas git clone was measured to produce git rev-parse --git-common-dir == ".git", a fully independent repository whose every write lands inside the workspace.

decisions.decision: The git child's environment is exactly PATH, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0, plus GIT_AUTHOR_DATE and GIT_COMMITTER_DATE on the commit call only. HOME is deliberately NOT allowlisted. Committer identity is passed as -c user.name=... -c user.email=... in argv. No git config is written at repository, global or system scope.
decisions.rationale: Measured on the real binary (git version 2.55.0, resolved under the devbox nix profile): clone, checkout -b, add and commit all succeed with an environment of PATH plus the two GIT_CONFIG_* pins and no HOME at all. Excluding HOME is therefore not a guess but the strongest available property, and strictly stronger than forge.go, which must allowlist HOME because the gh CLI reads its own store: with no HOME the adapter cannot reach the user's credential store even in principle, and internal/runner/source_guard_test.go TestNoCredentialStorePathReferencedInRunnerNonTestFiles already forbids naming such a path in a literal. Pinning GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL and GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM to /dev/null gives a hermetic configuration without mutating any config file, which is what "do not mutate git config at any scope" requires. Dates come from the injected clock so a commit is reproducible without a wall-clock read inside the adapter. GuardEnvironment's allowlist check and GuardCommand's secret-shaped-value check (internal/runner/secret_guard.go L12-43) run on this exact set; none of these names matches the secretName pattern.

decisions.decision: Every git child that can write runs inside NamespaceConfinement, whose Workspace is the Execution's own workspace directory. Probe runs first and a failure is a hard, reported failure: no child is started unconfined, ever. Only git --version may run unconfined, as an environment identifier read that writes nothing.
decisions.rationale: Measured inside unshare --user --map-root-user --mount with /tmp bind-mounted onto itself and remounted read-only and the workspace bind-mounted read-write, exactly as NamespaceConfinement.wrap builds it: git clone --no-hardlinks from a local bare origin into the workspace succeeded; git rev-parse --git-common-dir returned ".git"; checkout -b, add and commit succeeded; a write to the origin directory failed with EROFS; a write to /tmp failed with EROFS; and git push origin <branch> to that same file-path origin failed at "remote unpack failed: unable to create temporary object directory" -- the kernel refuses the remote write, independently of d4's argv allowlist. Two further properties fall out of the same mechanism at no cost: because wrap seals the top-level ancestor of the workspace read-only, a child confined for one Execution cannot write into a sibling Execution's directory, and because the origin lives under that sealed ancestor the clone source is structurally read-only. The fail-closed idiom is V2-046's, already stated in ProcessSupervisor.Run (internal/runner/supervisor.go L46-55) and in ErrNamespaceUnsupported's doc comment.

decisions.decision: A working copy lives at <workspace_root>/<execution_id>/source, created by the existing Workspace.Create(execution_id) followed by the clone into the source child; the confinement's Workspace is <workspace_root>/<execution_id>. internal/runner/workspace.go is a prohibited path and is not modified. Alongside the copy the adapter writes a plain-text descriptor naming increment_id, execution_id, repository_id and created_at. Discard removes the tree, is idempotent, and refuses any root that fails the same escape check Workspace.Path applies. SweepWorkingCopies(active) removes every workspace child whose execution id is not in the active set and is called at Runner start.
decisions.rationale: Workspace already owns the only validated per-Execution path in the codebase (internal/runner/workspace.go L31-65: single-segment id, no symlink, no escape, 0700), so reusing it means the working copy inherits four checks that are already proven rather than a second implementation of them. Nesting under the Execution directory rather than beside it is what lets the confinement seal one Execution without naming any sibling. The descriptor exists so a sweep can attribute an orphan to an Increment without consulting the Control Plane, which is exactly the state a crashed Runner leaves behind; it carries no credential-shaped field, so internal/runner's AST source guard stays green.

decisions.decision: The working copy's owner is the Execution, and that is what guarantees it never outlives the Increment: domain.Execution carries IncrementID (internal/domain/model.go L244-247), an Execution belongs to exactly one Increment for its whole life, and a working copy is never shared between Executions -- a retry gets a fresh clone. Nothing keyed by increment id alone is ever created on disk.
decisions.rationale: The non_goal is "do not let a working copy outlive the Increment that owns it", and a lifetime is only really bounded when the structure makes the longer life unrepresentable. Keying on the Increment would allow one directory to survive across Executions and to be reachable after the Increment was abandoned; keying on the Execution makes the directory unaddressable without the Execution id and removable by the same terminal transition that ends the Execution. The crash case is then a sweep over one directory level rather than a reconciliation against the Control Plane.

decisions.decision: Verification splits in two. Git-level integrity verification is EXECUTED in this task: after the commit the adapter runs status --porcelain=v2, diff --exit-code HEAD, rev-parse HEAD and the base, fsck --no-progress --connectivity-only, and cat-file on the committed tree, and returns a bounded IntegrityObservation. Project-level verification (running the cloned project's own build or test command) is DECLARED on the port as RunProjectVerification and fails closed with ErrProjectVerificationNotWired, starting no process.
decisions.rationale: Executing the Git-level check is not optional: a commit that was never verified to be complete and clean is precisely the plausible-looking unmeasured value docs/policies forbids, and every command it needs is already in d4's allowlist and writes nothing. Executing an arbitrary project command is a different animal: it is unbounded in cost and duration, it is the surface the CostLedger, the provider preflight and the standing-authorisation records exist to govern (internal/runner/costledger.go, internal/contracts/provider_preflight.go), and wiring it here would smuggle a second uncontrolled execution path past those gates. Declaring it with a fail-closed sentinel keeps the seam visible and testable now -- the refusal is asserted, and an AST control proves the method contains no exec construction -- which is the same honesty the application layer already practises with ObservedNotImplemented (internal/application/repository.go).

decisions.decision: Two clone sources, strictly separated. Inside make check the origin is a local bare repository created at test time by the real git binary in t.TempDir(); no fixture repository, pack file or bare directory is ever committed to this repository, and make check reaches no network. Outside make check, one live check is gated on AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_GIT=1 together with AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_GIT_CLONE_URL, which the owner supplies; it clones anonymously over https with --depth 1 --no-tags and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0. If the gate is set and the URL is absent the check FAILS rather than skips.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/validation.md L84 requires real git, a real kernel namespace and real signals in the integration test and forbids counting a skip as a pass, while L17-18 refuses to let automated tests and live exercise substitute for each other -- so the deterministic regime must not need the network and the live regime must not be deterministic. The environment-variable gate is the measured house pattern (internal/runner/forge_live_test.go L25 and L42-45, internal/runner/provider_live_test.go L43), and devbox run --pure strips the environment so a gate cannot fire by accident. Committing no git fixture is a hard requirement, not tidiness: validation.md L187 records that gitleaks git scans every ref, so a probe commit that reaches this repository's refs keeps the gate red -- the working copy must always be a separate repository in a temporary directory. Requiring an owner-supplied URL rather than hardcoding one follows validation.md L124's demand for an owner-designated target and avoids assuming a repository's visibility; a hardcoded default would make the check's meaning depend on an unmeasured fact.

decisions.decision: The Requirement-to-Repository association is a write-once side record, domain.RequirementRepositoryLink{RequirementID, RepositoryID, AssignedAt, RequestedBy}, declared in internal/domain/repository.go with its own ValidateRequirementRepositoryLink, and persisted behind one new member interface on the unit of work. internal/domain/model.go, control.go and lease.go are prohibited paths and gain no field. Service.Capture writes the link, in the same transaction, when the new optional CaptureRequest.RepositoryID is supplied.
decisions.rationale: The precedent is explicit and in the ports file already: ControlRequestedByRepository exists because "domain.ControlIntent itself is immutable, proven-closed M1 surface ... so who requested a given revision is tracked here rather than as a new field on that struct" (internal/application/ports.go L181-189). Requirement and Increment sit in internal/domain/model.go, the M1 closure surface this task may not touch, so the same shape applies for the same reason. Writing it in Capture is what the assignment's "follow Service.Capture's ceremony" means literally: Capture is where a Requirement comes into existence and therefore the only point at which the association can be write-once. Keeping it optional is what lets every pre-existing test keep passing unchanged with its assertions untouched.

decisions.decision: The association is NOT a Requirements slice on the Repository aggregate, and not a field on domain.Increment.
decisions.rationale: Two measurements against it. A slice on Repository grows without bound and would make every Capture a write to one Repository document, serialising intake per repository and burning the Installation's bounded Firestore mutation budget on a list append -- the same contention argument that put RunnerObservation and RepositoryObservation in their own records rather than on their aggregates. It also inverts the direction the model states: docs/architecture/domain-model.md L52 hangs the association off the Requirement, and internal/scheduler already carries Requirement.RepositoryIDs (internal/scheduler/scheduler.go L57), so a Requirement-keyed record is the shape the rest of the system already reads. An Increment field is unavailable regardless: internal/domain/model.go L234-242 is a prohibited path.

decisions.decision: The Repository detail view's fourth observable moves from unobserved to measured: RepositoryBacklogView gains a repository-scoped Requirement count (with a Truncated flag at the bound) while keeping InstallationScope exactly as it is, and RequirementView and RequirementDetailView each gain repository_id with omitempty. The count is read with a single-field equality query on the link record's repository id; firestore.indexes.json is not modified and no composite index is introduced.
decisions.rationale: internal/application/repository_test.go TestRepositoryDetailRendersAllSixDeclaredObservables L320-326 asserts today that the backlog is ObservedUnobserved with a reason and that the Installation-wide count is reported under its own scope name -- that is the assertion this task flips, and it is the one V2-064 recorded as the remaining unobserved item. omitempty on the row field is the measured house idiom for an absent measurement (requestedByView returns nil rather than an empty object, internal/application/readmodels.go), so an unlinked Requirement reports no repository instead of a guessed one. The query shape is chosen against the store: internal/store/firestore/store.go already runs bare single-field equality queries (Where("index_lease_id", "==", ...) at L850 and L896) with no entry in firestore.indexes.json, whose declared indexes cover only outbox and leases, so a single-field equality query needs no index change while any composite query would.

decisions.decision: application.ServiceConfig.RepositoryID is DELETED, not populated. The three consumers stop reading process configuration: Plan sets the canonical target's RepositoryID from the captured Requirement's link, the Control-Intent snapshot path resolves it from the lease's Increment to its Requirement to the link when no canonical target is stored, and Heartbeat's target carries no repository at all, by design and with a test that says so. cmd/control-plane/main.go is not edited and cmd/** stays a prohibited path.
decisions.rationale: Re-measured on this tree: ServiceConfig is declared at internal/application/service.go L150-154 with the RepositoryID field at L152; it is read at L451 (Heartbeat's target), L751 (Plan's canonical target) and L1140 (the ControlIntent snapshot fallback); cmd/control-plane/main.go L172 constructs it with InstallationID and LeaseTTL only; internal/domain/control.go L138 compares target.RepositoryID against the scope value. A grep of all 31 ServiceConfig literals in the tree finds not one that sets RepositoryID, so deleting the field changes no behaviour and cannot break a caller -- and it removes a field that lies rather than leaving one that has to be remembered. Populating it from an environment variable would be worse than the bug: an Installation registers many Repositories (that is what V2-064 built), so a single per-process repository id would make a ScopeRepository intent match the wrong repository instead of none. The repository id must come from the aggregate graph inside the transaction, which is exactly where Plan and the snapshot path already are. Heartbeat is the honest exception: HeartbeatRequest (service.go L370-374) carries no increment and no lease, and a Runner is not repository-bound, so attaching a repository to a runner-scoped observation would make a repository-scoped stop silently apply to unrelated work.

decisions.decision: The repair is proven by a test that makes a ScopeRepository Control Intent actually match: register a Repository, capture a Requirement naming it, plan an Increment, request a repository-scoped graceful stop naming that repository id, and assert both that the stored canonical target's RepositoryID is that id and that domain.ControlApplies holds for it -- with a negative control (a different repository id does not match) and a positive control (the assertion on a non-empty RepositoryID, which is what fails on today's tree).
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/validation.md's standard is that a claim is only made by a verdict that was actually produced, and "the scope is no longer dead" is a claim about matching, not about a field being set. internal/application/repository_test.go TestRepositoryControlGateDeniesUnderStop already proves the registration-side gate; this is its Increment-side counterpart, and the negative and positive controls are what stop it passing vacuously. internal/domain/control.go is untouched: matching already works, it has simply never been given a non-empty value to match.

decisions.decision: Two verification regimes, strictly separated. Inside make check: the port's refusal paths (non-absolute path, wrong basename, disallowed subcommand, non-allowlisted environment name, escaping ChangeSet path), the real-git real-namespace integration of clone/branch/change/verify/commit/discard/sweep against a locally created bare origin, the required positive control that the same outside-workspace write succeeds when the namespace is not applied, the link's domain closure and its write-once conflict, both stores, the API and OpenAPI contract, the owner console render, and the ScopeRepository matching proof. Outside make check, gated: the one anonymous live clone of an owner-designated URL.
decisions.rationale: This mirrors dp-v2-064 d16 for the same reasons and adds the one validation.md L84 requires by name: the positive control in which the write outside the workspace succeeds without the namespace, without which the EROFS result proves nothing about the namespace. Every deterministic item is reachable with no network; every live item is unreachable without one.

decisions.decision: Nine evidence records, one per component whose roots this task touches: domain, application, store-memory, store-firestore, api, web, contracts, runner, docs. Each records the execution environment identifiers -- machine and kernel from uname -srm, go version, devbox environment, and the resolved absolute git path with its version -- and each component key is read from make evidence-keys on the final green tree after the evidence commit.
decisions.rationale: docs/architecture/validation.md L252-253 makes the evidence key a per-component value read from the final green tree, so one record per component is the only grouping in which each key means what it says; dp-v2-064 d17 already settled this shape for the same nine components. The git absolute path and version are execution-environment identifiers for the same reason the gh version is one in V2-064: the claim is about a real binary on a real kernel, so the binary and the kernel have to be named. control-plane's key can move without its roots changing because contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is one of its declared contract_dependencies -- record it, do not repair it, ci/components.json is V2-045's.

decisions.decision: contracts/release-contract/** is untouched and no capability declaration is weakened, narrowed or reinterpreted. This task does not claim cap-autonomous-resolution. It removes the "no working copy exists" and "the repository control scope is dead" conditions; it does not remove the "no change reaches the forge" condition, which is V2-072's.
decisions.rationale: dp-v2-064 d18 set the rule and the reason: the declaration must not be rewritten to match the result, and moving the release contract is the coordinator's act, not the implementer's. Claiming the autonomous-resolution capability here would be false on its face, since nothing this task produces is visible outside the Runner's workspace.

decisions.decision: V2-071 belongs in the surface-widening serialisation chain and is proposed for position 2: V2-064 (done) -> V2-066 (running) -> V2-071 -> V2-069 -> V2-067 -> V2-073 -> V2-068 -> V2-065. The coordinator confirms the placement.
decisions.rationale: Measured overlap: V2-071 must touch internal/application/ports.go, service.go, readmodels.go, internal/store/memory/store.go, internal/store/firestore/store.go, internal/api/api.go, internal/web/owner.{js,html} and contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml -- the same cluster every task in the chain touches, so it cannot sit outside. Position 2 rather than last for three reasons: V2-071 is the only unblocker of V2-072 and therefore of the whole outcome sentence, so five unrelated widenings ahead of it delay the only path to a committed change; it repairs a live defect that every later task's target construction inherits, and repairing it once before those tasks is cheaper than revisiting each afterwards; and its footprint in the shared files is small and additive -- one field on captureBody, one field on two view structs, one member interface, one appended owner-console block -- so rebasing five successors onto it costs less than rebasing it onto five predecessors.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_GIT=1 -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_GIT_CLONE_URL=<owner-designated> -- go test -count=1 -run TestGitCloneLive ./internal/runner
uname -srm and git --version recorded in every evidence record
git diff --stat over internal/domain, plus the before/after top-level test count per touched package
risks: The execution environment's kernel may refuse unprivileged user namespaces, which makes the gate-bearing integration test unrunnable. It was measured to work here (unshare --user --map-root-user --mount succeeded and the EROFS refusals were observed), but a different machine may differ. A skip is never a pass: stop and escalate with the recorded kernel identifier and Probe's reason.

ProcessSupervisor.Run calls Confine.Probe on every invocation, so a working-copy sequence pays one namespace probe per git command. The cost is bounded and measured, but it must be logged as an observation and never asserted as a duration threshold.

The link record makes Capture's transaction read a Repository, which adds a read to the intake path. If the Installation's bounded quota reservation is affected the leg must be measured, not assumed; ReserveQuota already runs inside the same transaction.

A test that leaves a working copy behind, or a fixture bare repository that gets committed, turns gitleaks red for every later commit on the branch (validation.md L187). Every temporary repository must live in t.TempDir() and no git fixture may be committed.

Deleting ServiceConfig.RepositoryID is source-compatible only because no caller sets it; if the implementer finds a caller that does, the deletion is wrong and the task must stop and escalate rather than silently keeping a dead field.

Making the backlog's repository scope measured flips an existing assertion in internal/application/repository_test.go, so that test's name must stay and its meaning must change deliberately and visibly; silently deleting it would hide the transition.

A new import edge from internal/runner or internal/application can trip V2-045's manifest surface check. ci/components.json is a prohibited path, so a red manifest check is a stop-and-escalate, never an edit.

The live clone check depends on an owner-designated URL and on anonymous read access to it. If neither is available the live leg is simply not run and is recorded as not run; it must never be reported as passed, and no local or emulated clone may be recorded as satisfying it.
